title: Asynchronous startup can publish a superseded session
test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "a WHIP start aborted while transport.connect() is pending gives its transport up at once", "a WHIP start aborted while transport.connect() is pending publishes no session when connect() completes", "a stale transport.connect() completion after a replacement WHIP start leaves the replacement session as it is", "a stale video produce() completion closes only its own producer and never touches the replacement session", "a stale audio produce() completion closes only its own producer and never touches the replacement session", "a WHIP offer without a DTLS fingerprint gets 400 and leaves no transport on the room or in its media pipeline"
proof: The tests run the real WHIP router on a real HTTP server with fake mediasoup transports whose connect()/produce() wait on deferred promises. As in mediasoup 3.27.1, the fake's close() drops its dtlsstatechange listeners without emitting, and a connect() or produce() already pending still resolves afterwards (Transport.close() removes the channel subscription and does not reject pending requests; the worker answers them in order). With the unchanged lib/whipRoutes.js all six failed: after a client abort during connect(), room.whipTransport still pointed at the closed transport and the pipeline still owned it; when that connect() resolved, the cancelled start set whipSessionId ('a3763d11f726b865' !== null) and registered a WHIP resource with no client; after an abort and a replacement POST, the stale connect() overwrote room.whipTransport with the closed transport-1 (so the replacement's DTLS 'connected' would have been ignored); a stale video or audio produce() completing after an OBS reconnect called ownWhip('video-producer'|'audio-producer', staleProducer), which closed the replacement's producer, and then nulled the room field; the 400 for a missing fingerprint left room.whipTransport on the closed transport. After the fix: an isCurrentStart() check (not cancelled, room.whipGeneration and room.whipTransport still this start's) runs after connect() and publishes nothing otherwise; releaseWhipTransport() clears room.whipTransport and the pipeline's ownership together in cancelPendingStart, the post-connect check, the 500 path and the missing-fingerprint 400; commitProducer() assigns a produce() result and calls ownWhip() only while the session is current and DTLS connected, else closes only that producer. node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 17/17; tests/roomMediaPipeline.test.js 12/12; npm test 1061/1061; lint and typecheck pass.

title: Producer creation failure after DTLS connect is only logged, leaving a half-initialized session that never goes live and is never torn down
test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "a rejected video produce() tears the WHIP session down instead of leaving it half started", "a rejected audio produce() after the video producer tears the whole WHIP session down, video producer included", "DTLS failing while produce() is pending leaves the session disconnected, and the grace timer then closes it" (node:test mock timers); baseline "WHIP happy path: 201, then DTLS connected creates both producers and goes live" passes before and after
proof: With the unchanged lib/whipRoutes.js the three tests failed: after a rejected video produce(), and after a rejected audio produce() following a successful video one, the transport was still open ('the transport is closed': false !== true), the resource stayed registered and the video producer stayed owned by the pipeline; the error was only logged. With DTLS 'failed' emitted while the video produce() was pending, the later completion set room.whipConnected = true (true !== false), emitted new-producer events and prewarmed the relay, so the grace timer would have found a connected session and never closed it. After the fix the connected branch's catch calls teardownGeneration('producer creation failed'), the one generation-scoped helper (also used at grace expiry): when the session is still current it stops the relay, runs closeWhipSession (producers, transport and resource released), sets fallbackAvailable false and emits host metrics; a stale generation does nothing. The tests assert the transport and every producer closed, room fields null, the resource unregistered, the pipeline owning no WHIP transport or producer, whipConnected false, the last host-metrics call made after the teardown, and no new-producer event or relay prewarm. whipConnected is set only if the generation is current and DTLS is still connected after every await; after the DTLS failure the late producer is closed and the mocked grace timer then tears the session down. The added guard on the DTLS failed/closed branch and the grace-timer callback (current generation and transport only) has no test: mediasoup never emits dtlsstatechange for a transport the server closed (check 08), so a stale transport cannot reach that branch.
